"executive_summary": "The NCI's Clinical Proteomics Tumor Analysis Consortium (CPTAC) has performed large-scale proteogenomic characterizations of multiple cancer types, from which gene/protein regulatory networks have been derived to provide system-level understanding of the molecular regulatory mechanisms underlying cancer. While these co-expression networks contain rich information for identifying active pathways and oncogenic drivers, they are challenging to visually communicate due to their large dimensions and complicated topologies. Existing network data visualization tools are mainly used for communicating networks as static 2D images in print publications, and are not well suited for user-initiated interactive network explorations. To address these needs, the authors introduce ProNetView-ccRCC, an interactive web-based network exploration portal for investigating the phosphopeptide co-expression network inferred based on the CPTAC clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) phosphoproteomics data. ProNetView-ccRCC enables quick, user-intuitive visual interactions with the ccRCC tumor phosphoprotein co-expression network comprised of 3,614 genes, as well as 30 functional pathway-enriched network modules. Users can interact with the network portal and can conveniently query for association between abundance of each phosphopeptide in the network and clinical variables such as tumor grade. The portal is an open-access freely available resource at http://ccrcc.cptac-network-view.org/. The tool was implemented by building on the Three.js framework, which provides an interface for WebGL, and by calculating the network layouts using 3D layout algorithms within iCAVE, a desktop-based tool developed earlier for the stereoscopic and immersive exploration of networks. The portal runs on all modern web browsers without the need for any additional plug-ins. In conclusion, ProNetView-ccRCC provides a free, open access and custom environment for the interactive exploration of CPTAC ccRCC networks and their associated meta-data, and the authors anticipate that it will facilitate researchers from a wide spectrum of computational skill levels to conduct their own analyses on the rich CPTAC ccRCC network data, and share and communicate their results.",

summary.title: ProNetView-ccRCC: A web-based portal to interactively explore clear cell renal cell carcinoma proteogenomics networks
summary.authors: Selim Kalayci; Francesca Petralia; Pei Wang; Zeynep H Gümüş
summary.executive_summary: The NCI's Clinical Proteomics Tumor Analysis Consortium (CPTAC) has performed large-scale proteogenomic characterizations of multiple cancer types, from which gene/protein regulatory networks have been derived to provide system-level understanding of the molecular regulatory mechanisms underlying cancer. While these co-expression networks contain rich information for identifying active pathways and oncogenic drivers, they are challenging to visually communicate due to their large dimensions and complicated topologies. Existing network data visualization tools are mainly used for communicating networks as static 2D images in print publications, and are not well suited for user-initiated interactive network explorations. To address these needs, the authors introduce ProNetView-ccRCC, an interactive web-based network exploration portal for investigating the phosphopeptide co-expression network inferred based on the CPTAC clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) phosphoproteomics data. ProNetView-ccRCC enables quick, user-intuitive visual interactions with the ccRCC tumor phosphoprotein co-expression network comprised of 3,614 genes, as well as 30 functional pathway-enriched network modules. Users can interact with the network portal and can conveniently query for association between abundance of each phosphopeptide in the network and clinical variables such as tumor grade. The portal is an open-access freely available resource at http://ccrcc.cptac-network-view.org/. The tool was implemented by building on the Three.js framework, which provides an interface for WebGL, and by calculating the network layouts using 3D layout algorithms within iCAVE, a desktop-based tool developed earlier for the stereoscopic and immersive exploration of networks. The portal runs on all modern web browsers without the need for any additional plug-ins. In conclusion, ProNetView-ccRCC provides a free, open access and custom environment for the interactive exploration of CPTAC ccRCC networks and their associated meta-data, and the authors anticipate that it will facilitate researchers from a wide spectrum of computational skill levels to conduct their own analyses on the rich CPTAC ccRCC network data, and share and communicate their results.

Research Context
The NCI's CPTAC has performed comprehensive proteogenomic characterizations of tumor samples from breast, colon, ovarian, and kidney cancer patients. Co-expression networks derived from proteomics and phosphoproteomics data revealed regulatory relationships between proteins and posttranscriptional modifications (PTMs). These networks contain rich information for identifying active pathways and oncogenic drivers, but are challenging to visually communicate due to their large dimensions and complicated topologies. Current network data visualization tools are mainly used for communicating networks as static 2D images in print publications. These static tools are not well suited for user-initiated interactive network explorations. A centralized platform customized for CPTAC co-expression networks and associated meta-data is necessary.

Research Question And Hypothesis
The central need is an open community resource tool for intuitive visual exploration, interpretation, and communication of gene/protein regulatory networks. The authors hypothesize that an interactive 3D web-based portal will enable quick and easy interactions with the ccRCC phosphopeptide co-expression network and its meta-data. The authors hypothesize that users can query for proteins of interest, their neighbors, mappings to peptides or pathways, and apply filters on clinical variables. The authors anticipate that the portal will facilitate researchers from a wide spectrum of computational skill levels to conduct analyses and share results.

Methodological Details
The portal provides visual explorations of two network types: the phosphopeptide co-expression network of ccRCC tumors and 30 different network modules. The network characterizes co-expression patterns among 20,976 phosphopeptides in ccRCC. The network was derived using a random-forest based network construction algorithm based on phospho-peptide level data of 103 ccRCC samples. Two genes are connected if at least two phosphopeptides mapping to the two genes are associated to each other. Network modules were derived by using the Glay clustering algorithm. 30 modules containing at least 20 genes were identified and each was presented as a different module network. For each module network, pathway enrichment analysis was performed via Fisher Exact test. The final portal comprises 3,614 genes and 30 functional pathway-enriched network modules. The network layout was calculated using 3D layout algorithms within iCAVE. The 3D exploration capability was implemented by building on the Three.js framework, which provides an interface for WebGL. Multiple client-side Javascript libraries were utilized to handle various user interaction events in real time. The web interface styling primarily utilized Bootstrap v3.3.7, integrated with some styling of their own. The portal runs on all modern web browsers without the need for any additional plug-ins.

Procedures And Architectures
The ProNetView-ccRCC landing page provides the global ccRCC tumor phosphoproteomics co-expression network and links it to functional network modules. Users can interactively explore the large and dense topology of the whole ccRCC phosphopeptide co-expression network in 3D by rotating and zooming in/out the view. Six modules within this network were significantly associated with biological pathways, as highlighted within the network using different coloring of nodes. Users can easily query for genes of their interest in the network. Searching for the oncogene ERG highlights the corresponding node in red in the network exploration panel and identifies it as a member of the Angiogenesis enriched module network. The query returns the list of genes whose phosphopeptides were directly connected to ERG and provides the association of its corresponding phosphoprotein with tumor grade. The association of ERG's phosphoprotein with tumor grade has a p-value of 0.003 and FDR of 0.118. Users can click on a module name to explore a module network of interest and its associated meta-data in detail. Node sizes are proportional to the number of connections to let users easily identify the genes that are more central than others. Users can hover their mouse over a node to display the gene name of the phosphopeptide, and click on the node to display the associated gene-level meta-data in a separate panel. ERG is directly connected to 11 genes within the same module and maps to 5 different peptides. Users can click on the Heatmap link, which directs them to the ProTrack tool, which provides a web-based interface to explore ccRCC multi-omics data through interactive heatmaps. Users can construct a simple query for genes with similar association to tumor grade by specifying the phenotype of interest (grade) and the FDR cutoff value (FDR= 20%). Genes that satisfy these metrics are listed in the text box and are highlighted in the network exploration panel in red. Users can click the Reset button to return to the original network display. ProNetView-ccRCC displays and provides interactive exploration capabilities for any pathway enriched in a network module. Figure 3A displays the interactive table listing the enriched pathways, sorted by their p-values, associated with module 18. Clicking on a pathway name returns the list of associated genes in a textbox and highlights them in the network exploration panel in red.

Figure 3A displays the interactive table listing the enriched pathways, sorted by their p-values, associated with module 18. Clicking on a pathway name returns the list of associated genes in a textbox and highlights them in the network exploration panel in red. The tool runs on any modern web browser without the need for installing any specific plugins or libraries.

Interpretation And Theoretical Implications
ProNetView-ccRCC provides a free, open access and custom environment for the interactive exploration of CPTAC ccRCC networks and their associated meta-data. The tool facilitates researchers from a wide spectrum of computational skill levels to conduct their own analyses on the rich CPTAC ccRCC network data. The tool enables researchers to share and communicate their results. The portal helps understand the phosphopeptide network in the context of markers of user interest to help guide hypothesis generation for future studies. The portal enables intuitive visual interactions with the ccRCC tumor phosphoprotein co-expression network comprised of 3,614 genes, as well as 30 functional pathway-enriched network modules.
